confirmed_problem_statement: The project is a locally hosted price‑comparison agent that takes a list of product URLs as input and returns a ranked list of vendors showing each vendor’s price, shipping cost, and a direct purchase link. It will first try public vendor APIs for price data and fall back to web‑scraping (using tools such as Playwright or BeautifulSoup) when APIs are unavailable. An LLM running on the user’s local server via Ollama will be employed to normalize product titles and perform enhanced product‑matching across sites, ensuring that the same item is compared even when descriptions differ. The novelty lies in the LLM‑driven matching layer that improves accuracy over traditional string‑based methods. The solution targets the e‑commerce domain, using open‑source libraries and a self‑hosted LLM to respect privacy and run entirely on the user’s local server.
search_queries_used: LLM‑driven product title normalization for e‑commerce price comparison using self‑hosted models
Integration of Ollama self‑hosted large language models with web‑scraping fallback (Playwright/BeautifulSoup) for vendor API missing cases
Automated extraction of shipping costs from e‑commerce webpages via hybrid LLM and scraping techniques
Hybrid API‑plus‑scraping architecture with ranking engine for vendor‑wise price and shipping aggregation

papers.title: Using LLMs for the Extraction and Normalization of Product Attribute Values
papers.authors: Alexander Brinkmann; Nick Baumann; Christian Bizer
papers.why_relevant: Directly addresses Subagent 1's missing LLM‑driven product‑title normalization layer by presenting a concrete LLM‑based pipeline for extracting and normalizing attribute values from noisy e‑commerce titles, which can be adapted to run on a self‑hosted Ollama model.

papers.title: Webscraper: Leverage Multimodal Large Language Models for Index-Content Web Scraping
papers.why_relevant: Provides a detailed framework for LLM‑augmented, dynamic web‑scraping that can serve as the automatic fallback to Playwright/BeautifulSoup when vendor APIs are unavailable, exactly filling the scraping‑fallback gap identified by Subagent 1.

papers.title: AXE: Low-Cost Cross-Domain Web Structured Information Extraction
papers.why_relevant: Introduces a cost‑effective pipeline for extracting structured fields (price, shipping cost, purchase link) from arbitrary e‑commerce pages, directly solving the shipping‑cost extraction and link‑harvesting components missing in the current open‑source landscape.

papers.title: Method for Aggregating Unstructured Data Using Large Language Models
papers.why_relevant: Describes an LLM‑centric aggregation engine that consolidates heterogeneous product data into a ranked list, matching Subagent 1's requirement for a vendor‑wise price ranking module with direct purchase links.

papers.title: EPM-RL: Reinforcement Learning for On-Premise Product Mapping in E-Commerce
papers.why_relevant: Presents a reinforcement‑learning approach for on‑premise product mapping that outperforms heuristic string matching, offering a concrete algorithm to enhance the LLM‑driven matching layer envisioned in Subagent 1.
